subject: StellarCare private deployment: degraded p95 latency and rising 5xx — urgent
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@stellarcare.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: carlos.ruiz@stellarcare.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production alert — high p95 and 5xx spike on private cluster

Hi Tessa / Rishi,

We're seeing a sharp degradation in the StellarCare production inference cluster running in our VPC starting ~15:40 UTC (11:40 PT). Key observations: 
- P95 token latency jumped from ~180ms to ~2.8s for text-generation endpoints between 11:40–12:10 PT.
- 5xx rate for /v1/generate rose to ~6% (baseline <0.2%).
- Sustained drop in throughput; GPUs show queue buildup and occasional worker restarts.
- No config changes on our side during the window.

We've attached a diagnostic tar with system logs and agent traces (stellarcare_diagnostics_20260614.tar.gz) and included a small kernel syslog excerpt. Can you confirm whether this is something on Redwood's side (serving runtime / model variant / routing) or the private runtime in our VPC? This is affecting several customers and the VP of Eng (Laura Chen) asked for an update within the hour.

Thanks — Asha
[Attachment: stellarcare_diagnostics_20260614.tar.gz (120MB)]
[Attachment: kernel_syslog_excerpt.txt]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert — high p95 and 5xx spike on private cluster

Team — looping in SRE and CS leads.

Immediate asks:
- David: triage kernel/syslog and GPU agent traces from the tar. Look for OOM kills, NVLink/GPU ECC errors, or host-level throttling.
- Monica: confirm whether any model-routing fallbacks or quantization rollbacks happened in the last 6 hours.
- Rishi / Hannah: prepare a short exec note for StellarCare (what we know, what we'll do, ETA). Laura Chen is on the thread — they want a 1-hr update.

Suggested immediate mitigations (if David confirms host memory pressure):
- Reduce batch size to 1 on impacted routes and enforce a per-worker concurrency cap.
- Temporarily pin traffic to lower-memory model variant (if quality acceptable).
- If worker processes are unstable, plan a rolling drain/restart across their GPU pool with throttled concurrency to avoid cold-cache penalty all at once.

I'll take ownership on the customer communication. Rishi — we should prepare a small goodwill credit if SLA impact confirmed.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert — high p95 and 5xx spike on private cluster

Quick triage notes after unpacking diagnostics (attached excerpt and full tar to our support ticket SUP-1234):
- Host: observed repeated kernel OOM-killer entries on two GPU nodes (gpu-node-12, gpu-node-15) between 11:35–11:55 PT. Processes killed were torch processes of the serving runtime.
- NVLink messages and a burst of GPU driver resets in syslog on gpu-node-15; possible transient firmware issue compounded by high memory fragmentation.
- Agent telemetry shows workers accumulating large kv-cache sizes; there was a sudden spike in long-context user requests (several >8k tokens) at 11:30 which likely caused unexpected memory pressure.

Immediate actions taken (in order):
1) Reduced per-request max_length to 2048 for generation routes for StellarCare via a routing override.
2) Lowered default batch size to 1 and enforced worker concurrency cap in their dedicated pool.
3) Triggered a rolling restart of affected nodes (drain -> restart -> uncordon).
4) Opened SUP-1234 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234) and attached diagnostics.

Short-term mitigation rationale: reduces peak memory usage and prevents immediate OOMs. Expect p95 to begin improving within 10–20 minutes of full pool stabilization; 5xx rate should drop as killed processes are replaced.

Next steps (recommended):
- Schedule a firmware check and NVLink probe for gpu-node-15; possible hardware flake.
- Add guardrail in routing to reject requests exceeding 6k tokens for private deployments by default (configurable per-customer).
- Implement a kv-cache pre-warm and eviction policy that favors small-batch tail latency.
- Post-incident, run replayed trace set to quantify quality impact of fallback model variant.

Attachments: kernel_syslog_excerpt.txt (excerpt), diagnostic tar uploaded to SUP-1234.

— David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kernel_syslog_excerpt.txt]

Thanks for the quick triage and the mitigation steps. We can confirm the per-request limits reduced the immediate pressure — p95 is down to ~420ms in the last 12 minutes, 5xx rate falling.

Two asks from our side:
1) ETA on a full root cause and timeline for permanent fixes (firmware check + routing guardrails). We have scheduled a customer town hall at 14:00 PT tomorrow and need at least a short remediation plan.
2) Executive-level bridge: Laura Chen (VP Eng) has asked for a 30-minute bridge with Redwood leadership to understand SLA exposure and compensation. Can you confirm who from Redwood exec/SRE will join and proposed windows?

Also, please confirm any temporary credits if the final incident postmortem confirms SLA breach — we will need that information for our procurement team.

Best,
Carlos
Carlos Ruiz
Infra Lead, StellarCare Health
